races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a modest OR of 73, stepping up from 8-10f to 1m4f which is a potential positive given staying pedigree; Charlie Fellowes has a modest 14-day record but the horse has placed at this trip, and Good to Firm ground suits per sim-going history.

runners_data.name: Zurna
runners_data.note: Best recent form is a second over 10f on Good ground, which translates well to today's conditions; Dylan Hogan takes over and the step back to a sensible field size suits this hold-up filly who will want a clear passage in the Epsom straight.

runners_data.name: Celestarak
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good ground but the runner list flags a tendency to fade in the finish, and his natural hold-up style means he will be ridden from well off the pace rather than the midfield position shown on the map — a position from which he will need a strong, sustained run rather than a sprint finish to land this.

runners_data.name: Society Girl
runners_data.note: A 59-day absence is a notable concern for Ed Walker's filly, and her history shows a slide down the placings over 10-12f; though her true style is hold-up, she will be further back than the map suggests, making her reliant on a strong sectional finish that her form does not yet clearly evidence.

runners_data.name: Darkest Red
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's front-runner has placed four times from five starts at 10-12f and arrives here as the sole pace-maker in the field; his STYLE_FIT tag notes he is out of the role the map assigns him only in the sense of the wider field context, but in practice he will lead from the front and his class at OR 62 looks competitive in this modest handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Darkest Red is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press him, will stride into an uncontested lead from the off over Epsom's 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground. The remainder — Tai Hang Pegasus, Zurna, Celestarak, and Society Girl — are all hold-up or prominent types by nature, meaning the pace Darkest Red sets will be unchallenged and entirely self-regulated, likely producing a steady-to-moderate gallop that keeps his rivals in a tight bunch behind. Celestarak and Society Girl are flagged as redistributed hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map; in reality both will be ridden from the back, meaning Darkest Red's lead is even more secure than a small field might suggest. This race shape — a lone, ungrouped front-runner dictating tempo against a field of closers who must make ground on a flat track with no false pace to exploit — strongly favours Darkest Red's front-running profile and any hold-up horse who possesses a genuine, sustained finishing kick rather than a sharp sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Darkest Red Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Darkest Red settles into an uncontested lead and dictates a comfortable, measured gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: He travels alone throughout the 1m4f, setting a pace that suits himself rather than his rivals, and arrives at the two-furlong pole with energy reserves that a pressed leader would not have; his recent sequence of runner-up finishes over 10-12f in Good and Soft ground confirms he stays and competes at the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Darkest Red's solo lead becomes too slow, bunching the field and allowing the closers to deliver a sustained late challenge on the flat Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: A crawl-to-sprint dynamic gifts the hold-up horses a clean run in the straight with the race strongly in the balance; Zurna's recent second over 10f on Good and Tai Hang Pegasus's placed form over similar trips give them the stamina profile to capitalise when the tempo finally quickens in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types — Celestarak or Society Girl — secures a more forward position than expected and delivers a sustained run from mid-race.
scenarios.body: Celestarak's winning run over 12f on Good going shows the trip is in range, and a prominent position from the outset would negate the style-fit discount attached to his redistribution; however both horses carry the caveat of being out of natural role and their finishing tendencies suggest this scenario demands near-perfect execution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely too slow and a late finishing burst from a true hold-up horse catches a tiring Darkest Red inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Society Girl's stamina over 12f and Tai Hang Pegasus's previous placed effort on Soft ground provide late-race interest, but neither has shown the explosive turn of foot that a pure late-pounce scenario requires, making this the least likely outcome in this configuration.

watchPoints.text: Darkest Red must be watched in the opening quarter-mile — if he is allowed to bowl along without any pressure, his energy expenditure will be minimal and a front-running win becomes the stand-out shape in this race.

Zurna and Tai Hang Pegasus are both hold-up types who will need a clear run in the straight; with four horses potentially racing in a bunch behind the leader, traffic at the two-furlong pole on Epsom's narrow finishing straight is a live danger.

Celestarak's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a critical concern over 1m4f — if his jockey Jack Doughty attempts to compensate by moving earlier than usual, it could create an uncharacteristic mid-race move that disrupts the pattern of the race.

Society Girl's 59-day break means fitness is an open question; Ed Walker has a strong overall 14-day record but watch the market move as a guide to whether connections believe she is fully wound up for this return.

The actual going is Good to Firm (not Good as stated in the race conditions) — all five runners have sim-going histories that include Good, but the firmer surface may stretch stamina reserves in the final furlong and reward the horse who has been least pressured through the race.

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Robert Dyas Partnership Handicap

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with a reliable late run; has placed twice over 7f on Good ground and the trip is clearly his friend, though the trainer's recent 0/5 in 14 days and a moderate form string (523-67) temper expectations.|

runners_data.name: Stenmark
runners_data.note: One win in 14 attempts on similar going is a concern for a horse being asked to lead from the front; the uncontested lead is the scenario that flatters him most, but that 0.93 STYLE_FIT flag and modest recent form (3-5538) mean this is not a lock even in the pace-dominant shape.|

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is operating at a respectable 6/35 strike rate over 14 days, and Silver Trumpet's one win at 7f on Standout ground and two places in 15 similar-going runs keep her honest; a prominent style suits a single-pacer race if she can avoid traffic.|

runners_data.name: Panelli
runners_data.note: 147 days off the track is the headline concern here — a fresh horse that has previously placed twice at 7f on Standout ground and drops back in trip; Stuart Williams at 1/18 in 14 days suggests the yard is not in a particularly hot vein, so fitness must be proven.|

runners_data.name: Jersey Maverick
runners_data.note: Compelling placed record (three seconds in last five) and does best when allowed to race prominently, but the field's pace configuration means he is likely operating further back than he wants — that displacement is his primary tactical hurdle today, not ability.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner (OR 62) but showed a win at 7f on Standout going in his last five; like Jersey Maverick he is a true front-running type nudged into midfield by the race shape, and Jim Boyle's recent 1/4 form is a modest positive but cannot overcome the positional compromise.|

races.paceDynamic: Stenmark is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead on early pace, should secure a clean, uncontested advantage from the gates on this Good to Firm Epsom 7f. The pace he sets is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than frantic, which classically suits a resolute galloper who can dictate tempo — however, his STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals he is operating slightly out of his optimal role and must be discounted accordingly in scenarios that hinge on that position holding. Jersey Maverick and Dandy Khan are both natural prominent types who cannot all sit where they want, so one or both will be shuffled back into a midfield slot they are not bred for tactically, weakening their prospects in shape-dependent scenarios. This race shape — a controlled single pace-setter, moderate tempo on fast ground over 7f — most favours genuine hold-up horses with a reliable late kick, particularly those with proven form at the trip on similar going.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stenmark controls, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Stenmark breaks cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead at a sustainable clip.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to press him, Stenmark can dictate every yard and arrive at the Epsom straight full of horse, making his rivals work to close on fast ground where Epsom's downhill 7f rewards horses already in front. His style is prominent-to-lead and this is the scenario where that tag costs least — a low-pressure front makes the STYLE_FIT concern minimal.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late closers swoop late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and Stenmark burns off his rivals with a contested early gallop.
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses get the true pace they need and can produce a sustained late run down Epsom's straight, with Potomac River and Panelli ideally suited to that profile given their genuine rearward styles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent pair fight back
scenarios.trigger: If Jersey Maverick or Dandy Khan manage to recover their natural position despite redistribution.
scenarios.body: One of the displaced prominent types scrambles to sit closer than the race map projected, benefits from a moderate pace, and challenges entering the straight with running still in hand.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket finish, pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Stenmark sets an unsustainably quick tempo and capitulates inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The field bunches as the leader fades and several horses finish in a tight group, with Silver Trumpet's consistent placed record and Panelli's fresh return lending them marginal advantage in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Stenmark's early stride out of the gates is critical — if he misses the break even slightly, Jersey Maverick or Dandy Khan could steal the position he needs and the entire pace dynamic unravels.|

Jersey Maverick and Dandy Khan will both look to press forward early; watch for crowding or interference in the first two furlongs as two displaced prominent types compete for the same limited real estate.|

Panelli's 147-day absence means his first 2-3 furlongs will reveal whether he has come back fit — if he is sluggish early it confirms fitness concerns and he becomes a non-factor regardless of his placed profile.|

Good to Firm ground at Epsom's 7f favours horses with a high cruising speed rather than raw closers; Potomac River's hold-up style suits only if the pace is genuinely strong enough to create a meaningful gap to close.|

races.name: Robert Dyas Handicap

runners_data.name: Aberama Gold
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip on Good last time out and carries visor again; genuine hold-up operator who needs a strong enough pace to close into — the controlled shape here is the key concern, but course form is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Rage Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and can dictate fully uncontested; the STYLE_FIT flag notes a departure from natural role for this race shape, but that refers to the field context — if anything, securing the lead freely here suits; Good to Firm form (1W over 6f Good) supports.

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good for Attwater and arrives 16 days fresh; a genuine prominent type who will look to track Rage Of Thunder, and that position is entirely gettable in this field — distance and going both tick.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: Raced just 5 days ago, which is notably quick turnaround; headgear flag (p) and prominent style are fine for this shape but sim-going record is thin (1 run, no wins or places) and the recent heavy mileage warrants a note.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Standard and placed on Good, so handles the trip, but sim-going stats show 0W 2P from 5 on Good — capable of a late rattle from hold-up, and the 3yo weight advantage could matter.

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo whose true style is hold-up, repositioned to midfield on the map because the field is loaded with rear-runners; form figures of 0600-0 in recent starts are hard to overcome despite solid sim-going experience.

runners_data.name: Balon D'or
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been on Standard, making the switch to Good to Firm genuinely unexplored territory; a hold-up type pushed to midfield on the map, and both the going question and out-of-role placement make this a difficult profile to assess positively.

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good and placed at 6f on Good, so has live form angles; however, the apprentice booking (Ashley Lewis, 5lb claim) on a horse who is a true hold-up type in a pace-light race is a tactical challenge — the claim helps the weight, not the position.

races.paceDynamic: Rage Of Thunder is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Epsom, and with no natural rivals for the lead, Tom Queally can dictate a controlled, honest gallop without being pressured — a sustainable pace that will not overly soften the ground for closers. Twirler and Acclaimed Freedom will both push to be prominent, meaning the early fractions won't be crawling, but there is no genuine pace duel that will blow the race apart. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can accommodate: Ancient Times, Balon D'or, and Harry Brown are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and in this shape Rage Of Thunder and the two prominent types are most likely to actually secure their natural positions. With an uncontested pace-setter operating at a controlled clip on fast ground at a track where staying power over 6f is tested, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who travel close to the leader throughout, making a late sectional irrelevant by the time the field straightens.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rage Of Thunder Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Rage Of Thunder gets a clean break and settles into an uncontested rhythm, controlling the fractions throughout.
scenarios.body: Queally sets a fair but manageable gallop and the field is strung out before Tattenham Corner, leaving hold-up horses with too much ground to make up in the straight; prominent horses tracking the leader are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Override Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Twirler and Acclaimed Freedom both push hard to be up with Rage Of Thunder, injecting more pace than expected.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop increases the chance of the leader tying up late, handing the race to one of the prominent challengers who travels slightly off the pace before asserting; Good to Firm ground rewards those who have been travelling sweetly rather than grinding.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to burn off the leaders and create a gap for a hold-up horse to close into.
scenarios.body: Aberama Gold, who won over course conditions last time out, is the most credible beneficiary with form figures of 1 at 6f on Good and proven ability to finish strongly; King Of Chaos also fits this profile having shown a burst from off the pace on Good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If there are stumbles, traffic problems or a false break that scrambles the expected order from the outset.
scenarios.body: With multiple redistributed hold-up horses trying to advance from midfield and a compressed field, interference in the early stages could favour whoever avoids trouble irrespective of style; lower-weighted runners with tactical flexibility become live contenders.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rage Of Thunder's early strides — if Queally gets a clean break and establishes the lead unchallenged inside the first furlong, the uncontested pace scenario solidifies immediately and the race shape is effectively set.

Monitor Twirler and Acclaimed Freedom at the gate — if both push hard to go prominent, the early fractions will be sharper than the controlled-pace scenario assumes, increasing the chance of the leader tiring and a closer benefiting.

Aberama Gold's chance hinges entirely on pace: track him rounding Tattenham Corner — if he is in touch and travelling, his C&D win last time makes him dangerous; if he is detached, the lack of a strong gallop will leave him with no gap to close.

King Of Chaos is 3yo in a field of older horses and carries the lightest weight (131lbs) — watch his position at halfway, as a hold-up type on Good to Firm at Epsom over 6f needs to be closer than the map suggests to win from off the pace.

Harry Brown's jockey Ashley Lewis takes off 5lbs but the horse is a genuine hold-up type in a pace-light race — watch whether Lewis attempts to position closer than expected, which would signal the team are aware of the tactical constraint.

races.name: Betfred 'Nifty 50' Handicap

runners_data.name: Happy Banner
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter who has been running prominently and switches to the lead role here; five recent runs at 8f on Good/Standard-type going yield 0 wins and 3 places, suggesting a solid but limited ceiling, and the tp headgear may sharpen focus — the key question is whether a low-key solo lead translates to a winning performance.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good ground 10 days ago and steps up in trip here; the h headgear indicates he settles in rear, and his sole win at this type of going is encouraging, but the extra furlong and a race run at a controlled tempo may not generate the late sprint he needs.

runners_data.name: Darvel
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up specialist — his natural position is at the back of the field, and in a race where three genuine closers are competing for the same rear-quarter territory, he may well secure his preferred spot; two wins from 15 runs on similar going underlines the relevance of the conditions, though recent form (-95002) is subdued.

runners_data.name: Prodigal Son
runners_data.note: Showed 1 win from 3 runs on Firm ground and has been freshened up after a 39-day break; his natural inclination is to race from the rear, but the crowded hold-up zone in this field means he could be squeezed into a more prominent role than suits him — the style mismatch (STYLE_FIT 0.91) is worth bearing in mind.

runners_data.name: Buy The Dip
runners_data.note: One win and four places from 15 outings on similar going underlines his consistency at this level; a genuine hold-up horse, he holds reasonable claims if able to find his natural position at the rear, though the b headgear and a style fit flag (0.92) counsel some caution about the race shape suiting him fully.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Strong recent course and distance form with two wins and six places from 15 similar-going runs makes him one of the more statistically consistent horses in the field; racing prominently under Donagh Murphy (7), he is well-suited by a controlled pace and a one-paced Epsom straight that rewards those who travel smoothly into contention.

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the field (OR 72) and in solid recent form (5-5212); v headgear helps him switch off, he has won on Good ground at 8f, and a prominent racing style is perfectly calibrated for the likely race shape — Ralph Beckett's yard has been in fine form (9/59 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Ritaal
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old who holds up and has yet to win beyond 6f in the last five runs, with all five efforts on Standard ground; both the step up in trip and the surface switch to Good to Firm are unknowns, and the tb headgear combination suggests some temperament management is required — unexposed on this going, form is hard to pin down.

races.paceDynamic: Happy Banner is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rivals likely to push from the outset, should stride to the front unchallenged and control tempo through Epsom's testing undulations over 1m½f. Swiped and Play Me are the most likely horses to press from a prominent position, sitting just behind Happy Banner and potentially applying enough pressure to keep the pace honest without turning it into a sprint. The field carries a cluster of hold-up types — Darvel, Prodigal Son, Buy The Dip, and Ritaal — that are all mapped to midfield because there are more true hold-up horses than there is room at the rear of this eight-runner field; of those, Darvel and Buy The Dip are most likely to actually secure a rearward berth, with Prodigal Son potentially forced to race closer than ideal. With a single front-runner setting a measured, sustainable pace on Good to Firm ground at a track that rewards those who travel well and accelerate off a sound gallop, the race shape strongly favours prominent-racing types who can position themselves close to Happy Banner and pounce from a handy berth without getting trapped wide or too deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Banner dictates an unchallenged, even pace and the race is decided by a sustained burst from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Happy Banner sets a metronomic gallop over Epsom's unique contours, leaving those sitting just off the pace — principally Swiped and Play Me — perfectly poised to challenge with over a furlong to run; with no rival pressing from behind to disrupt the tempo, a horse that travels handsomely in second or third reaps the reward of a clean, uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Happy Banner's pace proves too well-judged and those in behind are unable to quicken sufficiently on the undulating Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: Happy Banner, given a soft lead throughout, conserves enough energy to repel challenges entering the final furlong; on Good to Firm ground that rewards a horse in a comfortable rhythm, the front-runner's stamina advantage over shorter-bred rivals becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses land late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the outset to compromise Happy Banner and the prominent brigade, allowing genuine closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Darvel or Buy The Dip, both true hold-up types who may actually find rear-of-field positions, would need a breakneck early gallop to launch a decisive late challenge from off the pace at Epsom, where the rising home straight tests finishing reserves; given both are tagged as redistributed and the pace is unlikely to be severe, this scenario is plausible only if the front-runners over-commit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic pace, midfield wins
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead unexpectedly and the race breaks up into a rough, fast-run affair from the outset.
scenarios.body: A scramble for position early on Epsom's downhill start could produce a fractured pace and a muddled run through the turn; however, with just one confirmed front-runner and a small field, this scenario requires an unlikely escalation from Swiped or Play Me into an all-out pace duel, and the structured nature of this field makes true chaos improbable.

watchPoints.text: Swiped carries the highest OR (72) and races with natural prominence under a trainer (Beckett, 9/59) and going record (5/6 on similar) that align precisely with the expected race shape — any market move should be respected.

Buy The Dip, Darvel and Prodigal Son are all genuine hold-up types competing for the same rearward positions; if all three jostle for the rear, at least one will be shuffled into an unfamiliar spot closer to the pace and is likely to race out of role.

Play Me's Going record (12/15 sim-going, 2W6P) is the strongest in the field for these conditions — uncontested by pace rivals, his prominent style could see him travel into a winning position without attracting the attention his record deserves.

Epsom's unique geography — sharply downhill for over half a mile before the camber and the final rising furlong — means a lone front-runner who over-settles on the descent could find Happy Banner difficult to reel in even if the finish time looks slow; monitor Happy Banner's price movements.

Ritaal's headgear (tb) and all-Standard-ground form profile create genuine going uncertainty on Good to Firm at Epsom — if the ground rides faster than the official description, unexposed types on this surface carry extra risk.

races.name: Betfred Play Fred's 5 Million Pound Handicap

runners_data.name: Living In Hope
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile trained by Harry Eustace; the step up to 1m2f looks a positive and the horse is bred to handle this trip, but in a race likely to be run at a steady pace by a sole front-runner, getting competitive from the rear will be the primary challenge.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, and Simon Dow's horse has won twice over 8f on Soft/Good — stepping up in trip and likely to find this ground on the quicker end acceptable; with no rival to press it, the chance to control every yard is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Don Pablo Colina
runners_data.note: Unclassified style leaves genuine uncertainty about where Neil Callan will position it; George Baker's stable is out of recent form (0/14 in 14 days) and three unremarkable runs over 8f on similar ground offer little encouragement for a step to 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Minerality
runners_data.note: Carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish and recent form figures of 8-9-6 are discouraging; Richard Newland and Jamie Insole's joint-trained runner has shown nothing on similar ground and the return after 31 days offers no obvious spark.

runners_data.name: Sweep In Time
runners_data.note: 190 days off the track is the immediate flag here — Tom Clover's two-year-old is also a genuine hold-up type whose natural rear-of-field role is harder to execute given the number of closers in this field; the combination of layoff, age, and positional squeeze makes a winning show a tall order.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's horse carries headgear and boasts a genuine prominent style that matches this race shape well; four placings from its last five runs (including two recent seconds on Good) suggest it handles conditions, though the 7lb claimer claim from Donagh Murphy needs to deliver cleanly at Epsom's tricky straight.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle is in sharp 14-day form (3/17) and the horse showed a placed effort over similar going, but it is a natural hold-up runner whose position in this field means it cannot drop to its favoured rear berth; the fade flags on its record further limit confidence in a finishing run.

races.paceDynamic: Sail On Sailor is the lone confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press them from the gate, is almost certain to dictate a steady, uncontested tempo over Epsom's 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground. Takeitorleaveit is the only other prominent type and will likely track Sail On Sailor in second, giving the race a clear two-tier formation with the remainder settled in behind. The field actually contains more hold-up types than can naturally sit at the rear — Sweep In Time and Cormorant Rock are true closers who have been mapped to midfield simply because the back of the field is congested, and they are unlikely to produce a true hold-up run from off a slow pace. A single front-runner controlling a modest gallop on a track that rewards tactical intelligence and finishing kick strongly favours horses who can sit handy and quicken — prominent racers and those with a sharp turn of foot from mid-division are the primary beneficiaries; genuine deep closers face an uphill task if the pace is never truly strong enough to bring them into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sail On Sailor Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Sail On Sailor secures the lead unchallenged and sets a controlled, even tempo that suits a prominent sit-and-kick finish.
scenarios.body: Sail On Sailor bowls along in front with Takeitorleaveit tracking closely, and the steady pace stretches the hold-up horses without ever generating the strong gallop they need; horses able to press from the front two positions pounce off the final turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Takeitorleaveit Strikes From Handy
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit uses its prominent style to track the leader and delivers a smooth challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: Takeitorleaveit's recent second-place finishes and habit of racing prominently mean it is ideally placed to challenge Sail On Sailor as the pace drops into the Epsom straight, where its ability to quicken from a handy berth becomes the key weapon.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough and a true hold-up runner finds a clean run through the field into the straight.
scenarios.body: Living In Hope is the most likely beneficiary, given it is the most credible of the hold-up types in terms of form trajectory, but this scenario depends on a pace scenario that the race shape does not naturally deliver, making it a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Front Two
scenarios.trigger: If Sail On Sailor or Takeitorleaveit suffer interference or traffic issues that shuffle the order entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A fractured mid-race pattern would hand an unexpected chance to a horse like Don Pablo Colina if it can slot into a prominent position, though its inconsistent recent form makes this a speculative scenario at best.

watchPoints.text: Sail On Sailor — if Paddy Bradley gets an uncontested lead at any pace, this horse becomes very difficult to pass; watch whether anything goes with it early from the gate.
Sweep In Time — 190 days off the track is a significant concern; watch the parade ring and early market moves to assess fitness before drawing conclusions about its involvement.

Cormorant Rock and Minerality both carry "fades in finish" flags and are natural closers displaced from their ideal position — if either gets squeezed for room in the straight, the race is likely over for them quickly.

Takeitorleaveit — carrying headgear (noted as "hg:p") and ridden by a 7lb claimer; watch whether it can actually secure second position behind Sail On Sailor from the gate, as that handy berth is the entire basis of its most likely winning scenario.

Don Pablo Colina — unclassified running style means Callan's positioning in the first two furlongs is worth watching; if it ends up deep in the field behind the hold-up cluster, its chance in a slow-run race effectively ends early.
